product_from_film: Juno is presented as a health companion that uses personal data to support daily planning and prepare a doctor-visit summary.
explains_well: The same person moves from a difficult evening at home to a prepared appointment, with the companion helping in both settings.
unclear: The floating character and panels do not show how the real phone app collects data, changes tasks or produces the doctor summary.
scenario: A woman struggles to reach care, accepts a health-journey prompt, receives a symptom/task suggestion and later gets help preparing for an appointment.
product_clear_basis: At 32–38s the companion shows health panels and captions describe a possible symptom flare and moving non-essential tasks; Juno is named on the final download card.

sound.detail: The draft opening describes no appointments for six months and a voicemail message. Later text largely follows the visible companion dialogue. It misrecognizes symptom flare and contradicts the visible nervous but ready caption, so captions take priority for those words. No validated listening.

categories.finding: Care-access frustration → opt-in → companion suggestion → rest → appointment preparation → doctor call → download.
A person on a bed surrounded by tissues creates a specific personal situation; the care-access barrier is supplied by the draft dialogue.
The companion task becomes clear at 35s through symptom/task captions; chronic-illness audience and Juno name are explicit on the ending card.
A blue panel rises from the phone, Yes is selected, a character/panels appear and the room darkens. Exact effects easing is unverified.
The same person and companion connect bedroom and waiting room; a black interval separates the two episodes.
Warm domestic light and soft gold character panels make the companion visually gentle; the initial blue prompt marks its arrival.
Dialogue captions explain the task while small biometric panels imply data context. The final app/category line is readable and held.
ASR adds the appointment barrier but contains clear recognition errors; visible captions support later dialogue. Voice qualities and mix remain unchecked.

categories.finding: Captioned companion dialogue makes the later support story readable silently; the opening access problem is less explicit without speech.
Close reaction shots keep the person central while floating panels sit beside the companion; no detailed summary document is shown.
The first 26s establish frustration and opt-in; two support episodes then lead to a 6s download card.
An initially troubled person later enters a doctor visit prepared; the film gives emotional closure without showing the summary itself.
Soft character design and warm lighting may suggest reassurance and companionship; actual viewer reaction is unmeasured.
One person, recurring character and consistent warm palette create continuity across two locations.
Symptom prediction, task changes and health-summary capabilities are dramatized claims. Clinical accuracy, data handling and integrations were not independently checked.
The cloud companion gives Juno a memorable character; a real app screen would better distinguish practical behavior from the visual metaphor.
Insert the actual task change or summary preview to connect the character story to app behavior.
